cvTemplates.POSE_HOLD: MediaPipe Pose (33 landmarks). Compute joint angles (hip-knee-ankle, shoulder-hip-knee), stance width (ankle distance / shoulder distance) and hold time. Score each frame 0-1 against the node's targets; a rep passes if the rolling average stays above the threshold for the hold time.
cvTemplates.JUMP_LAND: MediaPipe Pose. Detect takeoff/landing from ankle y velocity. Check both ankles land within the time window, knee flexion on landing, and knee valgus (knees closer than ankles).
cvTemplates.FOOTWORK_SEQ: MediaPipe Pose. Track ankle landmarks to segment steps (foot planted = ankle velocity near zero). Match the step order/pattern (pivot foot fixed, 1-2 vs hop, step-step-takeoff) against the node's expected sequence.
cvTemplates.LATERAL_SLIDE: MediaPipe Pose. Hip-center lateral displacement over time; flag frames where ankles cross or come closer than the threshold; track hip height variance (staying low).
cvTemplates.DRIBBLE_COUNTER: Ball detection (on-device YOLO/COCO 'sports ball' class or a color tracker as fallback) + MediaPipe Pose. Count bounces from ball-y local maxima (floor contacts), compare bounce apex height to knee/hip landmarks, find the contact hand as the nearest wrist at apex, and check head pitch for eyes-up.
cvTemplates.CROSSOVER_COUNTER: DRIBBLE_COUNTER + midline test: ball x crosses the line between the two hip landmarks below knee height, and the contact wrist alternates. Ball partly hidden behind the body + alternating wrist = behind-the-back; ball passing between ankle landmarks = between-the-legs.
cvTemplates.SHOT_FORM: MediaPipe Pose on a side or 45° view. At the set point: elbow angle (shoulder-elbow-wrist), elbow-under-wrist offset, knee flexion. At release: wrist above head, arm extension. After release: follow-through held (wrist stays high) for 1 s or more. Optional make detection: user drags a box on the rim and the app counts the ball passing down through it; otherwise one-tap make/miss buttons.
cvTemplates.REP_COUNTER: Generic counter: track a landmark or the ball around a reference point/line and count completed cycles (angle sweeps or line crossings).
cvTemplates.SEQUENCE: Chains the detectors above in order (e.g. DRIBBLE_COUNTER → FOOTWORK_SEQ → SHOT_FORM) with a max gap between steps. Each step must pass for the rep to count.
cvTemplates.QUIZ: No camera. Interactive court-diagram quiz (tap/drag players, pick the read) or short clip decisions. Used for IQ and team-concept nodes where pose tracking can't judge the skill.

designResponses: Lack of time (20/26) → every lesson uses short-form YouTube video (Shorts / clips under 4 min); no long videos.
Couldn't tell if improving (11) → CV form score per rep, saved history per node, and a simple progress screen.
Didn't know what to practice next / where to start (13 combined) → placement quiz + graph that always highlights 'next unlocked' nodes.
Burnout / lost interest (11) → XP, badges, streaks, short sessions; RPG-style tree.
Wanted live technique feedback (instrument player) → camera-based activity at the end of every lesson.
Notification feedback conflicted (one wants rare, one wants many) → let users pick reminder frequency; default to 1 daily reminder.
Cost / no paywall requests → keep the core tree free.

text.why: Every skill in basketball starts from a balanced stance. Triple threat means you can shoot, pass or dribble from the same position, so the defense has to respect all three.
steps: Feet a bit wider than your shoulders, toes pointing forward.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back, like you're about to sit in a chair. Chest up.
Hold the ball at your hip on your shooting side, both hands on it, elbows out a little to protect it.
Weight on the balls of your feet, not your heels.
commonMistakes: Standing straight up with locked knees
Holding the ball out in front where it can be poked away

visuals.caption: Look for: Butt down, chest up · Ball tight to the hip · Eyes up at the rim
